key_concept: Per the NCERT account of human evolution, Homo sapiens arose in Africa and moved across continents, and modern Homo sapiens arose during the ice age between 75,000 and 10,000 years ago.
steps: Statement I says modern Homo sapiens arose in Australia. NCERT says Homo sapiens arose in Africa and migrated across continents, developing into distinct races. Statement I is therefore incorrect.

Statement II says Homo sapiens arose around 75,000 to 10,000 years ago. NCERT says that during the ice age, between 75,000 and 10,000 years ago, modern Homo sapiens arose. Statement II is therefore correct as NCERT states it.
Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct, which matches Option (4).
final_answer: Option (4): Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
why_not_others: Options (1) and (3) fail because they accept Australia as the place of origin, but the origin is Africa. Option (2) fails because NCERT explicitly gives the 75,000–10,000 years ago (ice age) window for the rise of modern Homo sapiens.
common_trap: Students reject Statement II because they recall that anatomically modern humans are about 2–3 lakh years old, but NEET follows the NCERT line on the ice-age period of 75,000–10,000 years ago.
time_saving_tip: The word 'Australia' in Statement I makes it false at once ('Out of Africa'). That leaves only options (2) and (4), and recalling the NCERT ice-age dates confirms (4).
